data.one_liner: Pure Dart client for network ADB communication, including wireless pairing and shell access
data.what_it_does: Provides a Dart implementation of the Android Debug Bridge protocol over TCP, supporting wireless pairing, QR pairing, and shell streams. It can generate RSA keys for authentication and persist them if desired.
use_when: You need to control an Android device over the network from a Flutter or Dart app
You want to avoid native ADB binaries and use pure Dart
You need wireless debugging or QR pairing in your app
avoid_when: You only need to run ADB commands locally on the same machine
You prefer a higher-level backend SDK that hides ADB details
strengths: Supports Android 11+ wireless and QR pairing
Provides key generation and persistence helpers
weaknesses: Requires manual key persistence for repeat use
Limited to ADB protocol, not a full device management SDK
data.setup_notes: Add dependency, import package, create AdbCrypto, optionally persist keypair, then use AdbConnection or Adb.sendSingleCommand
